definition.name: schur_transform
definition.definition: The Schur transform Schur^d: (C^d)^{tensor n} -> bigoplus_lambda C^{dim(lambda)} tensor C^{dim(V_lambda^d)} is the unitary change of basis implementing Schur-Weyl duality. It maps the computational basis to the Schur basis, indexed by (lambda, S, q) where lambda is a Young diagram, S is an SYT of shape lambda (Specht/permutation index), and q indexes a basis of the Weyl module V_lambda^d. The output has three registers: Y (Young diagram label), P (permutation/Specht register), Q (Weyl/unitary group register). Key formula (Eq. 3.1): Schur^d rho^{tensor n} (Schur^d)^dag = sum_lambda |lambda><lambda|_Y tensor I_{dim(lambda),P} tensor nu_lambda^d(rho)_Q, where nu_lambda^d(rho) is a dim(V_lambda^d) x dim(V_lambda^d) matrix encoding rho in the lambda-sector. The Schur transform can be implemented efficiently in poly(n, log d, log 1/eps) time [BCH05, Har05].
